tasks.title: Promote the migration that adds the hryvnia equivalent columns to contracts
tasks.dod: The staged migration is live under a goose number from `mise run migrate:new`, applies and reverts cleanly, `mise run gen` leaves sqlcgen with the two nullable columns and every existing test stays green.

tasks.title: Model the official rate and compute the hryvnia equivalent with half-up rounding
tasks.dod: Unit tests prove the rounding table of AC-02 with exact integers, refuse a rate that is not a positive decimal with at most six fraction digits, and format a rate back to the published decimal with trailing zeros dropped.

tasks.title: Register the finance problem codes of PRD §5.1
tasks.dod: Each of the codes of PRD §5.1 (three at first; T14 added the fourth, so four) has exactly one constant whose string equals the catalogue, with its HTTP status in a registry, and a test fails when a code is missing or misspelt.

tasks.title: Merge the contract delta and stub the new finance operation
tasks.dod: The live contract holds `resolveContractUahEquivalent`, `UahEquivalent` and the changed `Contract`; `mise run gen` is clean; every contract answer carries `uah_equivalent: null`; the new operation compiles as a stub; lint and tests are green.

tasks.title: Read the official rate through the nbu-rates MCP server behind a finance port
tasks.dod: An adapter test against an in-process MCP server proves: a good `get_rate` answer becomes a `domain.Rate`; a `rate_not_published` tool error becomes `ErrRateNotPublished`; any other tool error, a refused connection, a wrong currency or date in the answer, a wrong source or a malformed rate become `ErrRateUnavailable`; the disabled provider always answers `ErrRateUnavailable`.

tasks.title: Store the hryvnia equivalent with a contract and set it only once
tasks.dod: Repository tests on a real database show: a contract created with an equivalent reads back with the same kopiykas and rate; one created without reads back with none; `SetUAHEquivalent` sets it on a contract that has none and changes nothing on one that has; another association's contract is not found.

tasks.title: Work out the equivalent when a foreign-currency contract is created, and never fail the creation over it
tasks.dod: Use-case tests with a fake rate port show: a EUR contract is stored with the equivalent of AC-01; a UAH contract is stored without one and the port is not called; when the port answers not-published, unavailable or blocks past 3 s the contract is still stored without an equivalent and the call returns within the budget.

tasks.title: Add the use case that works out a missing equivalent later, once
tasks.dod: Use-case tests show: a contract without an equivalent gets one; a contract with one is returned unchanged and the port is not called; a UAH contract, a not-published rate and an unavailable source return errors carrying `finance.equivalent_not_applicable`, `finance.rate_not_published` and `finance.rate_unavailable`; a lost race (`SetUAHEquivalent` updated nothing) returns the stored contract.

tasks.title: Return the equivalent on every contract answer and serve the «get it later» operation
tasks.dod: Module tests through the router on a real database, with a fake rate port, show AC-01 (create, get and list carry the same `uah_equivalent`), AC-05, AC-06 (also two concurrent calls → one stored value), every answer of AC-07 as `application/problem+json` with its `code`, and AC-08 (401, 403, 403 disabled, 404 for another association's id); the isolation test covers the new operation.

tasks.title: Wire NBU_RATES_MCP_URL from the environment to the finance module
tasks.dod: A config test reads `NBU_RATES_MCP_URL`; `cmd/api` builds the finance module with the MCP provider when it is set and the disabled one when it is not; the API starts in both cases; `mise.toml` sets the local default.

tasks.title: Prove the chain end to end against the real nbu-rates binary and a fake NBU
tasks.dod: One test builds `mcp/nbu-rates`, starts it on a free loopback port with `NBU_BASE_URL` pointing at an `httptest` NBU, creates a EUR contract through the finance module's HTTP surface and reads `uah_equivalent` = 6316388 at `50.5311`; a second contract for a day the fake does not publish is created with `uah_equivalent: null` and the later call answers `409 finance.rate_not_published`. No request leaves the machine.

tasks.title: Document the feature: Bruno request, environment variable, CLAUDE.md gotcha
tasks.dod: A Bruno request for the new operation sits next to the other finance requests; README and CLAUDE.md name `NBU_RATES_MCP_URL`, `mise run mcp:nbu` and what happens when the server is down; the root `.mcp.json` question is noted for the PR that owns that file.

tasks.title: Refuse a hryvnia equivalent that does not fit int64 instead of storing a wrong one

PRD AC-02/AC-07 + §5.1, the delta and the live contract name the new code; registry and catalogue tests cover 4 codes; a boundary test row exists.

tasks.title: Refuse redirects from the rate source and scrub each secret part of its address
tasks.dod: Review 2026-11-25 (round 3) finding 2: the MCP transport uses its own http.Client whose CheckRedirect returns http.ErrUseLastResponse; unavailable() removes the password, the username, every query value and the fragment as substrings, not only whole-URL spellings; a test against a server that redirects (e.g. /mcp → /mcp/) asserts the error text has no token, username, password or fragment.

tasks.title: Pin the call step against an address leak
tasks.dod: Review 2026-11-25 (round 3) finding 3: the vacuous "non-MCP answer" subtest of TestErrorKeepsCredentialsOutOfTheAddress is replaced by a stub that completes initialize and then drops the connection on tools/call (Post "<url>": EOF); with the scrubbing removed, that subtest fails.

tasks.title: Bound the rate lookup's HTTP requests so a hung source frees its socket
tasks.dod: Review 2026-11-25 (round 3) finding 4: every HTTP request of a lookup (including the notifications/cancelled POST and the DELETE the go-sdk sends on a context of its own) is bounded by the caller's deadline, or 3 s when it has none; a test against a server that reads each request and hangs asserts Rate returns within the caller's deadline and no request stays open on the server after it. (Amended while implementing: a client Timeout above 3 s still let Rate wait 3.6 s on the cancel notice, against AC-04's 3 s bound.)

tasks.title: Describe the adapter's own deadline and redirect refusal in the SAD
tasks.dod: Review 2026-11-27 (round 4) finding 1: sad.md §8 Timeouts says the app sets the 3 s budget and the mcprates adapter bounds every HTTP request (including those the go-sdk sends on its own context) by the caller's deadline, with a 3 s fallback, and refuses redirects; the mcprates row of §5 says it refuses redirects; tasks/T05-mcp-rate-provider.md no longer says the adapter sets no timeout; sad.md updated_at is bumped.

tasks.title: Bring the follow-up tasks into the epic's AC coverage and DAG

tasks.title: Make the hung-source test fail without the deadline transport
tasks.dod: Review 2026-11-27 (round 4) finding 3: the hung-source stub completes initialize and hangs on tools/call and notifications/cancelled; the test asserts Rate returns within the caller's deadline and no request stays open on the server after it; a case with context.Background() asserts Rate returns within about 3 s (fallbackBudget). Against the pre-T25 mcprates.go, or with deadlineTransport replaced by http.DefaultTransport, the test fails on every run (checked with -count=20). (Amended while implementing: go-sdk v1.8.0 sends no notifications/cancelled after an expired call; the request that hangs is the DELETE of session.Close, which the stub hangs too, and the test watches the server for 800 ms after Rate returns because that DELETE goes out after it.)

tasks.title: Redact the rate-source address structurally instead of masking substrings
tasks.dod: Review 2026-11-27 (round 4) finding 4: the lookup error no longer replaces secret substrings anywhere in the message; each URL in it is parsed and printed as scheme + host + path (no userinfo, query or fragment), with a placeholder that cannot collide with message text. A test with a one-character username, ?v=1 and ?x=end asserts the host (127.0.0.1:<port>) and the step stay readable and no NUL byte or secret reaches the error; the existing leak and redirect tests stay green.
